newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish cabinet to debate telecom sale next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish cabinet to debate telecom sale next week.

text.p: The government is likely to discuss a plan to sell a part of Poland's telecom monopoly Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) next week, the telecommunications ministry spokesman said on Monday.
"The telecommunications ministry's programme (to sell TPSA) is ready. The government debate on it should take plance next week," Marek Malinowski told Reuters.

He said that in drafting the privatisation programme, the ministry had taken into account studies by two investment banks, Schroders and CS First Boston, which had been picked as the ministry's official privatisation advisers in July.
He added it was too early to give any details.
TPSA's own sell-off plan provides for floating its minority stake on the Warsaw bourse and then possibly abroad, the firm's spokesman Krzysztof Bartnicki said.
"We have our proposals but the final decision (on the method of TPSA sell-off) rests with the government," he told Reuters.
Earlier this year, Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said that the sale of 10-15 percent of TPSA shares could bring $2 billion to $3 billion within three years.
Last year TPSA had revenues of 5.4 billion zlotys ($2 billion), of which it invested 2.1 billion zlotys, and netted 933 million zlotys.

According to telecommunications ministry estimates TPSA's revenues should rise steeply in the next 15 years. They should total 44.7 billion zlotys in the 1995-2000 period, 71 billion zlotys in 2000-2005 and 119 billion zlotys in the following five years.
The Polish law currently allows private operators to operate only on local telephone markets.
Telecommunications Minister Andrzej Zielinski has said TPSA will keep a monopoly in long-distance connections until after its privatisation.
Private operators will probably be allowed to operate international links by the end of 2002, according to Poland's obligations stemming from the World Trade Organisation membership.
